title: Using natural building materials
titleCn: 天然建筑材料建房方法

paragraphs.text: Section four. You will hear a lecturer talking to environmental science students about building methods using natural materials.
First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty on page seven.
Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

There is growing interest in building structures using natural materials these days. I'll begin this lecture by looking at how some of these materials work, some advantages and problems associated with each.

However, I must start by saying that all these materials and construction techniques require first and foremost a solid foundation, which will most often need to be made of concrete. Thus, the goal of using one hundred percent natural materials may have to be slightly compromised.

One type of natural building material is what is known as rammed earth. Rammed earth is a construction method whereby a framework constructed of wood is set in place to act as temporary walls, and then damp earth or soil is placed within this framework. As it is added, the earth is packed down and subjected to intense compression, either by hand or by using specialized machinery. Across parts of Africa today, you can see military fortifications built in this way over one thousand years ago, still standing in remarkably good condition.

The most appropriate type of soil for this construction method is one with a high concentration of sand in it, though other kinds of soil are sometimes successfully used. Rammed earth buildings are well suited to dry, arid climates.

Another form of natural construction is called the adobe method or sometimes the mud brick method. This utilizes bricks which can be made from a variety of soils but are most suitable when made from a soil rich in clay. The bricks have got to be carefully made to prevent them from cracking. The main advantage of this adobe brick method is that the materials are cheap and also that it's convenient for people in many geographical areas. Thus, adobe buildings have been traditional forms of construction in many societies and today can be found all over the world.
The construction method is also popular because making the bricks requires minimal training.

However, the adobe method does have its drawbacks. For proper preparation of the bricks, large quantities of water are required, and because these bricks are manufactured by hand, the process demands significant investment of time as well as labor, which can be backbreaking and exhausting.

A natural building material which has been popularized in the US is the use of straw bales to create walls. Straw is, of course, dried stalks of plants, especially tall grasses. The straw is shaped into large rectangular blocks called bales, tightly bound together, and these are excellent for use in the building of walls. When building with straw bales, the first thing that needs to be done is to construct a roof supported by poles so that work can continue even if it rains. Then the straw bales are stacked up to form walls. The bales are then coated with a layer of plaster which seals and protects them and keeps the insects out of them. The most common reason for their use in building today is the fact that they provide a very effective means of insulation for the building.

Another great building material is bamboo. This highly versatile plant is one of the fastest-growing plants in the world. One of its primary advantages is due to the hollow, round, and segmented shape of its individual stalks which give it its strength. And because of its light weight, it is easy to handle. A significant drawback, however, is that the large varieties of bamboo which are best suited for construction grow only in tropical and subtropical regions of the world. And also because it catches fire easily, bamboo can be problematic and potentially dangerous.
